title: "median() of integers returns an integer or a double depending on the number of values"
ref: NUM-06
categories: [Numbers]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'typeof(median(c(1L, 1L)))'
reponse: '"double"'

versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2022)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
typeof(median(c(1L, 1L, 1L)))
typeof(median(c(1L, 1L)))

identical(median(c(1L, 3L, 5L)), 3L)
identical(median(c(1L, 3L, 5L, 7L)), 4L)
```
:::

## Why

With an odd number of values, the median is the middle value: R returns it as is, hence as an integer. With an even number, it is the mean of the two central values, and `mean()` always returns a double, even when the result is a whole number.

The type therefore depends on the data, not on the code. Type-strict code (`identical()`, `vapply(..., FUN.VALUE = integer(1))`, a typed database column) passes on one sample and breaks on the next.

## The fix

Set the type of the result explicitly.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
typeof(as.numeric(median(c(1L, 1L, 1L))))
typeof(as.numeric(median(c(1L, 1L))))
```
:::
